title: TECHNICAL CUSTOMER SERVICE ADVISOR
description:
TECHNICAL CUSTOMER SERVICE ADVISOR
NORTH FAMBRIDGE, CHELMSFORD
CIRCA £35,000 + COMPANY BONUS

THE OPPORTUNITY:

Do you have an electrical background and enjoy helping customers understand products and solve technical problems?

Get Recruited is recruiting on behalf of an established engineering business for a Technical Customer Service Advisor to join its small, friendly team. You'll use your electrical knowledge to answer technical enquiries, support customers and keep their orders moving.

This opportunity would suit a Technical Support Advisor or Customer Service Executive with an electrical background who enjoys answering product questions and helping customers. You'll join long-serving colleagues in a business that values health, family and work, with regular team dinners and your birthday off.

THE TECHNICAL CUSTOMER SERVICE ADVISOR ROLE:

You'll combine the product knowledge of a Technical Support Advisor with the customer care and order administration skills of a Customer Service Executive.
- Handle customer enquiries by telephone and email, asking relevant questions to understand their requirements and provide clear, accurate advice.
- Explain electrical product functions and specifications, helping customers understand technical information and how components operate.
- Read technical datasheets, electrical schematics and connection diagrams to answer questions about relays, control circuits and associated components.
- Investigate product performance and fault enquiries, gathering information about the application, connections and symptoms to establish the next steps.
- Liaise with technical colleagues and the overseas manufacturing team to resolve complex questions, keeping customers informed throughout.
- Manage enquiries through the shared inbox, maintaining clear records and following outstanding queries through to resolution.
- Process customer orders accurately, checking product references, quantities and requirements before entering them into the order management system.
- Answer questions about availability, order progress and deliveries, coordinating with colleagues to resolve issues.
- Assist with picking and packing orders when required, contributing to the practical running of a small team.
- Adapt to new systems as the business introduces more automated ordering and customer administration processes.

THE PERSON:
- Experience as a Technical Support Advisor, Customer Service Executive or in a similar position supporting customers with electrical or electronic products.
- Alternatively, an electrical engineering background with experience explaining technical information to customers.
- A sound understanding of electrical components and how they function within a circuit.
- Confident reading electrical diagrams and technical datasheets, including supply voltages, relay contacts and connection arrangements.
- Clear communication skills, patience and a methodical approach to investigating customer problems.
- Strong attention to detail when processing orders, recording information and following up enquiries.
- As a Technical Customer Service Advisor, you'll be comfortable balancing technical enquiries, order processing and practical tasks within a small team.
- A relevant technical qualification is desirable, ideally in electrical or electronic engineering.
- Experience with relays, control panels or industrial automation products would be advantageous.

A Technical Support Advisor will bring experience investigating product questions; a Customer Service Executive will need the electrical knowledge to handle those conversations confidently.

TO APPLY:

If you're a Technical Support Advisor or Customer Service Executive with an electrical background, or an electrical engineering professional with customer support experience, we'd like to hear from you.

Please send your CV for the Technical Customer Service Advisor role via the advert for immediate consideration.

title: Fitness to Practice Administrator
description:
Job Title: Fitness to Practice Administrator

Location: Chelmsford campus

Start Date: ASAP

Proposed End Date: 23rd December 2026

Hours: 37hrs per week

Rate of pay: 16.19ph

Job Purpose:

To coordinate and oversee the University's Fitness to Practise processes, ensuring cases are managed efficiently, consistently and in line with regulatory, professional and University requirements. The role provides specialist administrative support, manages complex casework, and drives process improvements to maintain a high-quality service.

Key Responsibilities:

Act as the principal administrator for Fitness to Practise processes, coordinating the end to end administration of cases and ensuring compliance with University regulations, professional standards and statutory requirements.

Maintain and oversee the central record of all Fitness to Practise concerns, ensuring information is accurately recorded, monitored and reported, and that appropriate audit trails are maintained.

Monitor case progression and proactively manage Fitness to Practise workflows, identifying key deadlines, escalating issues where appropriate, and ensuring cases are progressed in a timely manner.

Coordinate and administer Fitness to Practise panels and associated meetings, managing complex scheduling requirements and ensuring arrangements comply with procedural requirements.

Arrange and support initial review meetings and Fitness to Practise hearings, including the preparation of agendas, meeting documentation and Microsoft Teams arrangements.

Provide specialist administrative guidance to academic and professional services staff, students and practice partners on Fitness to Practise procedures and processes, referring complex matters as appropriate.

Communicate with students throughout the Fitness to Practise process, including requesting statements, providing procedural information and ensuring that required documentation is obtained within agreed timescales.

Coordinate meetings between students and the Professionalism Lead, ensuring relevant information is available to support effective discussion and decision making.

Applicants must also possess strong IT skills. You will be expected to work in a polite, confidential, and discreet manner, respecting patients at all times. Key Duties and Responsibilities: Welcoming patients to the surgery in a professional and friendly manner Handling incoming telephone calls and booking appointments Processing incoming post and other communications Actioning tasks within the clinical system Processing referrals Undertaking a variety of administrative duties to support the smooth running of the practice Work in a polite, confidential and discreet manner, respecting patients at all times. Appointments & Communication Maintain and monitor the appointment system. Facilitate communication between patients and clinicians. Process messages, referrals, and documentation in line with Practice procedures. Administrative Support Manage incoming and outgoing mail and correspondence. File, scan, and code patient records and hospital letters accurately. Support clinical and administrative staff with general clerical tasks. Enter patient data and update records promptly and accurately. Registrations Manage patient registrations, temporary cover, and address changes. Handle private services, including payment collection and issuing receipts. Premises & Equipment Open and close the Practice premises securely, ensuring alarms and equipment are correctly set. Keep reception, waiting, and kitchen areas tidy and well-stocked. Ensure photocopiers, fax machines, and other office equipment are operational. Teamwork & Cover Provide cover during staff absence or annual leave. Participate in Practice meetings and training sessions as required. Confidentiality All Practice staff must maintain strict confidentiality regarding patient information and business operations. Confidential data must only be shared with authorised personnel and in accordance with GDPR, NHS guidelines, and the Practice's confidentiality policies. Health & Safety Follow all Health & Safety and Infection Control procedures. Identify and report hazards promptly. Keep all work and patient areas clean, tidy, and safe. Participate in relevant training sessions annually. Equality, Diversity & Inclusion Treat all patients, colleagues, and visitors with dignity and respect. Support and promote a culture of inclusion and non-discrimination. Be responsive to the individual needs of patients and staff. Remain vigilant and report any concerns or disclosures in line with the Practices safeguarding policies and procedures. Undertake mandatory safeguarding training and refreshers as required. Act as a responsible and trusted member of the Practice team, maintaining professional boundaries and understanding your role in protecting individuals from harm.
